_comment: Example ~/.pi/agent/models.json wiring the 'secrouter' provider that
pi/extensions/secrouter-auth.ts registers. That extension owns the OAuth login
(SecSSO device-code flow, per-user); THIS file owns the deployment-specific
baseUrl + model catalog, the same split models.md documents for Ollama/vLLM.
Usage:
export SECROUTER_SSO_DEVICE_URL=https://secsso.<domain>/realms/secrouter/protocol/openid-connect/auth/device
export SECROUTER_SSO_TOKEN_URL=https://secsso.<domain>/realms/secrouter/protocol/openid-connect/token
pi --extension ./pi/extensions/secrouter-auth.ts
/login secrouter        # SecSSO device-code login -- YOUR OWN token is used,
# not a shared/static key. pi stores + refreshes it in
# ~/.pi/agent/auth.json (0600) automatically.
/model                  # pick a secrouter/<id> model
oauth is intentionally NOT set on the provider entry below -- custom OAuth flows
only work via pi.registerProvider() in an extension, never as a models.json
literal (the only literal models.json accepts there is "radius", pi.dev's own
hosted gateway -- unrelated to SecRouter). See docs/models.md 'Value Resolution'
and 'Provider Configuration' for the full rules this file follows.
KIMI GUARD: this file registers ONLY the 'secrouter' provider. It does not
enable, override, or reference pi's built-in 'Kimi For Coding' provider
(PRC jurisdiction -- excluded from this suite's model defaults).
